summary.name: Fazm
summary.one_liner: Fazm is an open-source native macOS app that runs the real Claude Code and Codex agents with persistent sessions, one-click chat forking, and no auto-compacting, and can extend that loop to the browser, Mac apps, and Google Workspace by voice or text.
use_cases: Running Claude Code or Codex in a native Mac window instead of the terminal
Automating multi-step workflows across email, calendar, and spreadsheets
Forking a chat to explore alternate approaches without losing context
Driving browser and Mac apps by voice or text commands
Organizing files and folders on a Mac with an agent
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Fazm as a graphical front end for the real Claude Code and Codex agents on macOS, so the same agent loop used in the terminal runs in a native app. Sessions are persistent and survive a restart, and any chat can be forked in one click. The page states that auto-compacting is not used. Per the page, the agent can also reach into the browser, Mac apps, and Google Workspace, and it accepts voice or text input. A long list of example prompts shows tasks such as scheduling meetings, filing Jira tickets, organizing Downloads, and comparing prices, but these are marketing examples and the page does not document how each is implemented. The page says the project is fully open source on GitHub and lists it under AI tools on awesome-mac.
notable: Runs the real Claude Code and Codex agents in a native Mac app with persistent sessions that survive restarts
One-click chat forking and no auto-compacting
Voice or text control spanning browser, Mac apps, and Google Workspace
caveats: Page does not state pricing details beyond being open source
Platform support is described only for macOS; no Windows or Linux mention
Many example prompts on the page are marketing illustrations rather than verified results
